BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: BTECH   SEMESTER: III
BRANCH: MECH/PROD   SESSION: MO/2022

SUBJECT: PE214 METALLURGICAL & MATERIALS ENGINEERING

TIME: 2 HOURS   FULL MARKS: 50

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 50.
2. Candidates attempt for all 50 marks.
3. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
4. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
5. Tables/Data hand book/Graph paper etc. to be supplied to the candidates in the examination hall.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    CO BL
Q1 (a) Differentiate between  the  terms  ‘element’  and ‘component’  in  a
thermodynamic system with two representative examples for each.
[2] 02 BL1
 (b) State Gibbs phase rule, name the associated terms, and explain why melting
of a pure element is an invariant but that of a binary alloy is not an invariant
change. Can this rule be applied in continuous cooling operations?
[3] 02 BL3


Q2 (a) Draw the (A) [110] direction and (B) (201) plane in a cubic unit cell. [2] 01 BL3
 (b) Show with derivation that for hexagonal closed packed structure, the ratio
c/a is generally 1.633.
[3] 01 BL2


Q3 (a) Why is coordination number concept evoked only for ionic and not metallic
crystals?
[2] 01 BL3
 (b) (i) Why taking reciprocal is necessary for Miller indexing of planes?
(ii) Differentiate between edge and screw dislocation.
[1+2] 01 BL1


Q4 (a) A binary phase diagram comprises only two horizontal lines (neither inclined
line nor curves) as its liquidus and solidus lines. How is that possible? Please
offer your explanation for this unique type of a phase diagram.
[2] 02 BL3
 (b) Name the type of diagram which shows partial solubility in liquid and solid
state but has no invariant change for the entire alloy composition range.
[1] 03 BL3
 (c) Why is steel usually more ductile than cast iron at room temperature, but is
less suitable for casting than cast iron?
[2] 02 BL1


Q5 (a) State  two  characteristics  to  differentiate  between  pearlitic  and  bainitic
transformations, though both are essentially products of the same eutectoid
change.
[2] 02 BL3
 (b) For an Fe-1.15 wt.% C alloy, determine:
(i) the proeutectoid phase that forms,
(ii) the composition and amount of each phase present at 728°C,
(iii) the composition and amount of each phase present at 726°C
[assume eutectoid composition is 0.8 wt.% C and eutectoid temperature is 727
°C]
[3] 02 BL3


Q6 (a) Which of the following is NOT correct in terms of elastic modulus (E) among
the three (3) classes of pure engineering solids (namely, polymeric, ceramic
and metallic):
(i) Polymers usually have very high E,
(ii) Ceramics have much higher E than polymers,
(iii) E of metals is usually between that of polymers and ceramics,
(iv) Polymers usually have lower E than metals and ceramics.
[1] 03 BL3
     PTO






 (b) The neighboring grains or crystallites in the microstructure of a multi-phase
polycrystalline aggregate may differ in terms of:
(i) only composition,
(ii) only crystal structure,
(iii) only orientation,
(iv) composition, crystal structure and orientation.
[1] 02 BL3
 (c) Annealing twin is a
(i) volume defect
(ii) surface defect
(iii)  line defect
(iv)  point defect
[1] 02 BL1
 (d) Austenite in steel can transform on cooling to
(i) only one product phase aggregate
(ii) two possible product phases or phase aggregates
(iii)  three possible product phases and two phase aggregates
(iv)  four possible product phases
[1]  01 BL2
 (e) In Fe-Fe
3
C system, identify the ONLY correct statement from the following:
(i) Fe
3
C has body centered tetragonal structure
(ii) Ferrite has orthorhombic structure
(iii) Martensite is a phase aggregate
(iv) Both pearlite and bainite arise from the same invariant transformation
[1] 02 BL3


Q7 (a) Temperature is a state function, but mechanical strain is not – justify this
statement with proper logic
[2] 03 BL4
 (b) Name the invariant phase transformation that differentiates cast iron from
steel and mention the name and product (phases and phase mixture) of this
transformation.
[2] 02 BL3
 (c) Name the allotropic form of pure iron that is non-magnetic [1] 01 BL1


Q8 (a) The softest and hardest phases in mild steel are _____________ and
_____________, respectively
[2] 01 BL2
 (b) Segregate the following elements into two groups of austenite and ferrite
stabilizers in steel: Ni, Cr, Mn, C, W, Cu, Nb, V
Austenite stabilizers: _________________________
Ferrite stabilizers: ___________________________
[2] 02 BL2
 (c) Offer one reason why pearlite usually nucleate on prior austenite grain
boundary.
[1] 02 BL3


Q9 (a) Why does strength of a metallic alloy usually increase if average grain size is
decreased? What is this relationship called?
[2] 03 BL2
 (b) A silicate glass component (say cooking ware) develops greater thermal shock
resistance if it is partially devitrified (crystallized) – why?
[2] 03 BL3
 (c) How can a pure metal be strengthened (without changing composition)? [1] 02 BL3


Q10 (a) If four distinct phases are observed in a laboratory specimen of a binary alloy
made at one atmospheric pressure. Is such an observation possible? Explain.
[2] 01 BL3
 (b)
Calculate the volume change (in %) as FCC -Fe changes to BCC α-Fe. [Given
atomic radii of -Fe and α-Fe are 0.127 nm and 0.1241 nm, respectively.
[3] 02 BL2
